content_blocks.title: Project Overview & Therapeutic Concept
content_blocks.content: Project Title: ApoptoSENS (study finished, paper published). The project develops Chimeric Antigen Receptor Natural Killer (CAR-NK) cells engineered to selectively recognize and eliminate senescent cells, which accumulate with age and drive chronic inflammation, tissue dysfunction, and aging-related disease. The team identifies novel senescence-specific surface markers, validates them across models, generates monoclonal antibodies, and uses them to build CAR-NK constructs with improved precision and safety over existing senolytics. Target Indication: accumulation of senescent cells. Patient Population Size: not specified.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism of Action
content_blocks.content: CAR-NK cells are engineered to recognize senescence-specific surface antigens (e.g., SENS-1, SENS-2, SENS-3) that are absent on healthy cells. Upon binding the target, NK cells induce apoptosis in senescent cells, reducing SASP-driven inflammation and tissue dysfunction. This approach aims to improve precision and safety over existing senolytics.

content_blocks.title: Biological Target
content_blocks.content: Novel senescence-associated surface markers discovered in IMR-90 cells rendered senescent by ionizing radiation or doxorubicin. Top candidates include SENS-1, SENS-2, SENS-3, with SENS-3 showing the strongest early promise. Model system used: IMR-90 human lung fibroblast cell line. Senescence induction methods: ionizing radiation and doxorubicin treatment.

content_blocks.title: Team Information
content_blocks.content: Key Personnel: Dr. Amit Sharma, Project Lead, SENS Research Foundation. Affiliations: SENS Research Foundation, Senescence Immunology Research Group. Dr. Sharma holds a PhD from the University of Pune and conducted prior postdoctoral research at the Buck Institute. Team expertise areas: cellular senescence biology, immunology and immune aging, NK-cell and CAR-cell engineering, target discovery and antibody generation, translational aging-related therapeutics.
